steps.body: Trail markers, page numbers, temperatures — stories move along lines all day. Find the start and the move, and the line does the rest.
steps.narration: Trail markers, page numbers, temperatures — stories move along lines all day. Find the start and the move, and the line does the rest.

widget.prompt: Maggie hikes from marker 35, thirty meters onward: three ten-hops.

commonLandings.feedback: A three-meter start — each leg of this hike is a full ten meters.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10, going forward. From 35, 3 hops land on 65.
widget.successFeedback: Marker 65 — the story's hike, walked as jumps anyone could re-tell.

predict.prompt: A story says Maggie walks BACK toward the trailhead. Which way on the line?
predict.reveal: Back toward the start means smaller markers — a leftward, subtracting move, whether she turns around at marker 60 or marker 25.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2l story.
invariants: Position on the line IS the number: equal jumps cover equal amounts, and a journey's landing depends only on start, jump size, and direction for g2l story.
misconceptions: Treating marks as decoration — unequal spacing, jumps of the wrong size, or reading a start mark as a landing.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which change — start, jump size, or direction — would move the landing, and which would leave it alone?

widget.prompt: Maggie stands at trail marker 23 and hikes 10 meters onward. So 23 + 10 = ?

commonErrors.feedback: The hike moved FORWARD along the trail — the marker number grows.
One extra ten crept into the hike; measure just the 10 meters.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Walk the line: find the start mark, take the jumps one at a time, and read the mark you land on.
